extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners dealing with Korean (KIPO) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and examining Korean patent application documents (cover sheet, abstract, specification, drawings) and for satisfying enablement/support requirements under the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling applications filed by KIPO-affiliated personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person who works for a KIPO-affiliated organization (e.g. a prior art search institution) files a patent application while working for that institution, the examiner shall request a search to an outside prior art search institution and then perform examination accordingly; if the application can be granted, three examiners consult to decide allowance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a special procedural safeguard: use an outside prior art search and collective (three-examiner) decision-making to avoid conflicts of interest when applications originate from KIPO-affiliated organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to obtain a patent not subject to pledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The entitlement to obtain a patent shall not be the subject of a pledge; where a pledge is established upon the entitlement to obtain a patent, the pledge shall not be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: once a patent right is registered, a pledge can be established upon the registered patent right (see note about pledge on registered rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of patent application cover sheet (Article 42)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application cover sheet must state: (1) name and domicile of the applicant (or name and place of business if a corporation); (2) name and domicile/place of business of an agent if represented (and firm name/place and designated patent attorney if agent is a patent firm); (3) the title of the invention; (4) the name and domicile of the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet should also indicate applicant code, priority claim, claim on grace period disclosure exception, and request for examination. The cover sheet must be accompanied by a specification, drawings if necessary, and an abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract usage and limits (Article 43)
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract shall be used only for technical information and shall not be used to define the scope of the invention for which patent protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts are for ease of searching and disclosure of overview technical information; matters disclosed only in an abstract do not have the status of subject matter of another patent application and cannot be added to the specification by amendment. Poor or missing abstracts may trigger requests for amendment and, if unaddressed, may lead to invalidation of the application proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification composition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification filed with an application must contain the description of the invention and the claims, necessary drawings, and an abstract (claims may be submitted later by amendment within prescribed periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification serves as both the right document (defining scope) and a technical disclosure for third parties; follow Chapters 3 and 4 (descriptions and claims) for preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention: brevity, conciseness, identity
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention must be written briefly and concisely according to the subject matter of the invention and shall be identical in the application cover sheet and the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous or wordy titles. Do not include personal names, trademarks, nicknames, expressions indicating only abstract functions, or the word 'patent'. Where multiple categories (product, process, device, use) are claimed, use a concise title encompassing them (e.g., 'Paper, manufacturing process and manufacturing device thereof'). Amend title if claims change; examiners may suggest proper titles or amend ex officio in limited cases. An inappropriate title is not generally a ground for rejection except where clearly inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In the section for brief description of drawing(s), state what each drawing displays (e.g., 'Drawing 1 is the ground view of the whole assembly...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief description of drawings is inappropriate, handle similarly to inappropriate titles (notify applicant, suggest amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: when required and preparation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may be attached when necessary for explanation of the claimed invention; they must be prepared according to the guideline for drawings (Annexed Form No. 17 of Enforcement Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where drawings are difficult to prepare per the form (e.g., crystal structures, fibers, oscilloscope results), pictures may replace drawings if they clearly can be laid open in the Official Gazette; grayscale or color accepted if unavoidable. For utility model registration, drawings must be included (failure = illegitimate application returned). Irrelevant drawings may be indicated and notified; attachment errors that do not affect practice may be treated as references but not as grounds for rejection. Submitting new drawings by amendment may constitute adding new matter; examiners must be cautious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (Article 42(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the invention shall be written clearly and fully so that any person skilled in the art can easily practice the invention based on ordinary skill, the specification and drawings at the time of filing, without adding special knowledge or undue trial and error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement means a skilled person fully understands and reproduces the invention using routine skill at filing. The 'invention to be practiced' is interpreted as the invention recited in the claims; disclosure only in the description but not in the claims does not trigger Article 42(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject of practicing the invention (claims-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention that must be enabled is the invention recited in the claims; if an invention is disclosed only in the description but not claimed, lack of enablement for that unclaimed matter does not violate Article 42(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner assessment focuses on whether a person skilled in the art can practice the claimed invention as defined by the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'easily practicing' the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Easily practicing' means a skilled person fully understands and reproduces the invention with ordinary skill at filing time, without added special knowledge, undue trial and error, or repetitive experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delimits the threshold for enablement; speculative or unpredictable inventions requiring extensive experimentation fail enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for product inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For product inventions recited in the claims, the description must contain clear and full explanations enabling a skilled person to produce the product; generally the manufacturing method needs to be fully described unless the product can be manufactured based on spec and drawings with ordinary skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe roles and functions of each special technical feature. Also describe how to use the product unless use is obvious from spec/drawings and ordinary skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for method (use) inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For method inventions, the description must contain clear and full explanation enabling a skilled person to use the method; the roles and sequences of each step that specify the process should be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the method fully graspable from the disclosure so that it can be executed by a skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement for manufacturing method inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For manufacturing-method inventions, the description must enable a skilled person to produce a product by the manufacturing method; raw materials and a detailed series of steps must be fully described unless the product is readily understood from materials/steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the manufactured product clearly, and provide detailed steps and materials; omission risks lack of enablement for the method and produced product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enablement: chemical substance inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical substance inventions are not usually enabling by name or formula alone; detailed manufacturing methods and experimental confirmation/analysis are generally required (starting materials, temperature, pressure, inflow/outflow, and results of direct experiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed reaction conditions and experimental results unless a skilled person at filing would readily understand the reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enablement: medicinal (use) inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical/medicinal use inventions, the effect of the invention should be disclosed (medical data proving effect) or a description detailed enough to replace such data, except where the medical mechanism is clearly known prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of low predictability and reproducibility, experimental examples and data are important to satisfy enablement for medicinal uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special enablement: parameter inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions that include applicant-defined parameters (not generally used in the art), detailed technical content of the parameter must be described so a skilled person can realize the invention, including definition/technical meaning, numerical scope and reasons for limits, measurement method/condition/device, method of manufacturing products meeting the parameter, embodiments fulfilling the parameter, comparative examples not meeting the parameter, and relation between parameter and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parameter details are not explicitly stated but are clearly understandable from the filing-level skill, examiners should not find lack of enablement. The guidance lists seven specific content elements that should be provided for parameter inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of enablement and claim support (Articles 42(3) vs 42(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 42(3) (enablement) applies where a skilled person may not easily reproduce the claimed invention based on the description; Article 42(4)(i) (lack of support) applies where the claimed invention is not disclosed in the description or is outside the scope of what the description discloses to a skilled person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether claims are supported by the description by assessing if the subject matter of the claims is disclosed in the description for a skilled person. If description cannot be generalized to claimed scope, claims are not supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species support rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims recite a genus but the description only discloses species and the genus cannot be clearly recognized from species, Article 42(4)(i) applies; conversely, if description discloses only a specific embodiment and other embodiments in the generic claims cannot be easily practiced, Article 42(3) also applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Article 42(4)(i) or 42(3)(i) depending on whether the issue is lack of disclosure of the genus or lack of enablement of other embodiments within the genus; examples given for molding methods and oxygen-absorbing compositions illustrate these points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush/grouping support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Markush grouping is used in claims but the description only discloses embodiments for some constituents and not others so that a skilled person cannot easily practice the rest, an examiner shall notify rejection under Article 42(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If embodiments for the other members of the group are not disclosed in sufficient detail, lack of enablement/support will be found (example: nitration of substituted benzenes where only one substituent's behavior is disclosed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of terms between description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If terms used in the description and the claims do not clearly match, the examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(4)(i) because the claim is not supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure terminology in claims and description align so a skilled person recognizes the claimed subject matter in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description method and required sections (Article 21 Enforcement Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of the invention shall, in principle, contain: title; technical field; background art; prior art literature; summary of invention (including technical task, solution means, effects); brief description of drawings; detailed description for practicing the invention; industrial applicability; consignment number; sequence listing or free text. Sections may be omitted if not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose is to disclose technical advance and clarify technical matter and scope so third parties and examiners can easily understand the invention. The sections need not be separately prepared if overall disclosure suffices. If certain sections cannot be filled out, omission is permitted if the invention is understood from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of description method violations (filing-date-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of description method requirements constituted grounds for rejection or invalidation for applications filed before December 31, 2014, but for applications filed after January 1, 2015, they shall be subject to amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rule affects remedies: older filings could be rejected/invalidated; more recent filings get opportunity to amend the description to comply.
